newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares stronger on renewed interest.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares stronger on renewed interest.

text.p: Nigerian shares closed stronger on Monday as investors resumed buying, putting budget anxieties behind them, traders said.
The all-share index rose to 7202.79 from 7182.42 on Friday.
"With the worries over the 1997 budget behind them, investors are in the mood to trade now, especially with the continuity in economic policy of the government," one trader said.
After nearly three weeks' delay, the budget was released last week, ending investors' wait-and-see attitude.
Traders said renewed interest in previously falling stocks also buoyed activities.
Shares of tyre maker Dunlop and food giant Cadbury were in this category, closing five kobo and 10 kobo higher at 7.65 naira and 23.40 naira, respectively.
"Both stocks were deemed to have fallen to the lowest point possible," a trader said.
Activity also rose in the banking sector, strengthening the position of the nation's four biggest high street banks.
First Bank was 8.55 naira, up 10 kobo; UBA was 7.37 naira, seven higher, while Union Bank and Afribank each closed five kobo more, respectively, at 7.50 naira and 4.15 naira.
Insatiable demand for the shares of West African Portland Cement Company raised its price by 50 kobo to 51.50 naira although other equities in the sector fared less well.
Ashaka Cement was one of Monday's two losers, ending 10 kobo lower at 14.40 naira, one trader said.
Chemical and Allied Product was 20 kobo down on its falling profitability, closing at 4.59 naira.
Petroleum marketing companies had a bleak day as a fuel scarcity put their shares under pressure.
They recorded low price movements as Total and Mobil rose 10 kobo each to 63.20 naira and 54.85 naira, respectively.
